evals.prompt: we're about to redesign our subagent fleet — what does Anthropic officially recommend for subagent architecture, tool grants, and model selection? research this before we plan the redesign
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines covering separate facets (architecture/composition, tool-grant philosophy, model selection), states it will read references/official-sources.md before composing briefs, and outlines a synthesis plan naming both Consensus/best-practices and Contradictions/drift sections explicitly.

files.content:
# Model selection

Current pins (updated 2026-08-31):

| Agent role | Model |
|---|---|
| Hub | claude-opus-4-5 |
| Default spoke (code-implementer, test-author, etc.) | claude-sonnet-4-5 |
| Explore spoke | claude-sonnet-4-5 |
| Lightweight (linting, labelling) | claude-haiku-4-5 |

Rationale: hub maximises reasoning depth; spokes optimise cost and throughput.
Tiering reviewed when Anthropic releases a new frontier model.

expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines in the response, each brief covering a different named facet of the topic — architecture/composition patterns, tool-grant philosophy, and model selection guidance must each appear as a separate dispatch with a distinct one-line brief, not merged into one.

Every WOULD-DISPATCH brief names only sources from the official Anthropic domain allowlist (anthropic.com, docs.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com, or other Anthropic-owned domains listed in references/official-sources.md); no brief mentions third-party blogs, Medium, Reddit, Stack Overflow, community sites, or vendor comparisons.
The response states it will read references/official-sources.md before composing agent briefs to obtain the domain allowlist — it does not inline a self-derived allowlist or skip this step.

The planned synthesis structure names both a Consensus/best-practices section and a Contradictions/drift section explicitly; a response that names only a generic 'summary' without the contradiction-flagging step fails this criterion.
All WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before any synthesis plan or briefing structure is described.

The research plan explicitly references the seeded docs/contributing/model-selection.md to anchor which model-selection gap the research is closing — it does not plan the research in a vacuum ignoring the existing repo model pins.

evals.prompt: /researching-anthropic-guidance prompt caching — I want to know Anthropic's official recommendations before I redesign our prompt structure
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines covering different facets of prompt caching (cache-breakpoint placement, TTL/cost tradeoffs, API usage patterns, model-specific behavior), each restricted to Anthropic-owned domains, followed by a synthesis plan naming both Consensus/best-practices and Contradictions/drift sections explicitly.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet of prompt caching — cache-breakpoint placement, TTL and cost tradeoffs, API usage patterns, and model-specific caching behavior are the expected facets; no two briefs may cover the same facet.

Every WOULD-DISPATCH brief explicitly restricts its search to Anthropic-owned domains (anthropic.com, docs.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com, or other allowlisted domains); no brief names a third-party source, community blog, Stack Overflow answer, or documentation site not on the official allowlist.

The response indicates agents will write full findings to per-facet scratchpad files under a run directory and return only a compact digest to the hub — the full file contents are not repeated in each agent's return message.

The planned synthesis output explicitly names both a Consensus/best-practices section and a Contradictions/drift section as distinct headings; a response that merges these into a single 'summary' without naming the contradiction step fails this criterion.
WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before the synthesis plan is described; the response does not offer to write a docs/research/*.md snapshot file before the user explicitly confirms.

evals.prompt: is there an official Anthropic engineering blog post about building effective agents? I want a synthesized summary I can cite, and flag it clearly if anything in there conflicts with the newer subagent docs
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines across different effective-agent facets, with at least one brief explicitly targeting anthropic.com/engineering as a primary source, and a synthesis plan that names a contradiction-flagging step comparing the blog post against current docs with a note on which source is more authoritative.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet of the effective-agents topic — workflow vs agent patterns, tool design, orchestration, and evaluation are the expected facets; briefs must not all cover the same angle.

At least one WOULD-DISPATCH brief explicitly targets anthropic.com/engineering as a primary source for the blog post rather than relying on generic search ranking to surface it — the URL or path segment must appear in the brief.

Every WOULD-DISPATCH brief restricts sources to the official Anthropic domain allowlist; no brief directs a search at a third-party blog, community resource, non-anthropics GitHub repository, or any domain not on the allowlist in references/official-sources.md.

The synthesis plan explicitly names a contradiction-flagging step that compares the engineering blog post's guidance against current docs, and states that current docs take precedence over an older blog post when they disagree — a merged summary that averages both without naming precedence fails this criterion.

WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before the synthesis plan is described; the contradiction-checking step is named before the final briefing output structure; the response does not promise to write any repo file without explicit user confirmation.

evals.prompt: /researching-anthropic-guidance has Claude Code shipped anything in the last few releases around hooks or subagent tool grants? I want to know before we touch our hook config — see docs/harness/settings-snapshot.json for what we currently have
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines across different facets of recent Claude Code changes, with at least one brief explicitly naming the Claude Code CHANGELOG URL or the release-notes page as a first-class source to fetch directly, and a synthesis plan naming both Consensus and Contradictions/drift sections.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet of recent Claude Code changes — hooks/lifecycle events, subagent tool-grant behavior, and settings schema changes are the minimum expected facets.

At least one WOULD-DISPATCH brief explicitly names the Claude Code CHANGELOG URL (raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md) or the release-notes page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/claude-code) as a first-class source to fetch directly, not just a generic search that may miss it.

Every WOULD-DISPATCH brief that references GitHub scopes the search to github.com/anthropics/* or raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/* only; no brief directs a search at bare github.com, a third-party GitHub org, or any non-Anthropic repository.

The research plan explicitly references the seeded docs/harness/settings-snapshot.json hook entries (PreToolUse, guard-branch-isolation.mjs, guard-hub-src-writes.mjs) to frame which specific hook behaviors the research is meant to validate against recent official guidance.

WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before the synthesis plan is described; the planned briefing names both a Consensus and a Contradictions/drift section as distinct headings, not a single merged summary.
